```plato

    //==
    // # Triply periodic minimal surfaces
    //
    // The nodal implicits, each a short trigonometric sum whose zero level set
    // approximates a minimal surface repeating in all three axes
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triply_periodic_minimal_surface). They are
    // ordinary spatial scalar fields, so the marching cubes and sphere-tracing
    // paths already in the tree consume them unchanged.
    //
    // Turning one into a DISTANCE takes a Lipschitz bound: dividing an implicit
    // by an upper bound on its gradient magnitude gives a value that never
    // exceeds the true distance to its zero set, which is the LOWER BOUND
    // fidelity `implicit-sdf.concepts.plato` describes. Each bound below is the
    // summed coefficient of one partial derivative, lifted to all three by a
    // factor of the square root of three and scaled by the angular frequency.
    // They are honest bounds, not tight ones — the gyroid's is twice its true
    // maximum — so a sphere tracer takes short steps and never steps through.

    // The angular frequency of a period: one full cycle of the trigonometric
    // argument per Period of world distance. Precondition: period is positive.
    TpmsFrequency(period: Number): Number
        => Number.Tau / period;
```
